accent-strong-ink.displayName: Fired Clay Ink (accent text on neutral material)

display.purpose: Page titles (h1) in the sticky hero. Weight 800, -0.03em — the bold form's voice.

title.purpose: Section headings; on Overview they double as collapse controls.

label.purpose: Sidebar group labels and h3 — the only sanctioned uppercase tracked role.

shadows.name: whisper
shadows.purpose: Cards and search at rest. Derived from ink so it deepens in dark modes.

shadows.name: float
shadows.purpose: Popovers, menus, toasts — anything overlapping other content.

shadows.name: btn-glow
shadows.purpose: Primary buttons only — an accent-colored signature.

motion.name: motion-feedback
motion.purpose: Immediate feedback: colour, background, opacity, filter. Hover, press, selected, focus.

motion.name: motion-reveal
motion.purpose: Component reveal: opacity plus a 2-4px transform. Menu, tooltip, top-layer action palette, disclosure glyph.

motion.name: motion-continuity
motion.purpose: State continuity: opacity plus a 4-6px transform. Toast, pointer-started keeper dock, overlay entrance, and the manual left-pane material edge/content translation. A completed destination jump may compose three tokens into a non-blocking Ring and Wash locator with a 4px settle.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The only easing. Decisive out-curve, no bounce, no elastic.

motion.name: rejected
motion.value: routine layout animation, ambient looping motion, smooth scrolling, delayed state or focus
motion.purpose: D4-4 closed the vocabulary. The user-triggered Dashboard left pane publishes final layout once, then animates a flat material edge, content translation, and native-size sidebar opacity; disclosure folds, boot, responsive changes, and data rendering remain instant. P11-16 stages solid accent text before pending work, waits 180ms to avoid flashing on fast reads, and uses one 80ms compositor opacity reveal so main-thread pressure cannot suppress feedback. No pending state loops. test/smoke.mjs enforces it.

breakpoints.name: nav-compact
breakpoints.purpose: Navigation drops to the 60px icon rail. NAV_COMPACT_MAX in js/lib/nav-mode.js.

breakpoints.name: nav-header
breakpoints.purpose: Navigation becomes the anchored header switcher and content takes the full width. NAV_HEADER_MAX.

breakpoints.name: setting-row-stack
breakpoints.purpose: Container query on .setlist: a setting's control stacks beneath its label.

breakpoints.name: list-compact-actions
breakpoints.purpose: Container query on .tablist: action labels collapse to accessible icons. Wide rows default to names; users may choose icons everywhere.

breakpoints.name: stats-collapse
breakpoints.purpose: Stat grid drops from 4 to 2 columns.

components.name: Hero Search
components.description: The most important element on the page: one fixed-height 760px top-left sticky row aligned with the working collection. Results expand in a connected absolute overlay without moving collections or sticky headers. The interior is a continuous command ledger: square rows, a complete selection band, title then bounded source then plain-text outcome. Filter examples are borderless syntax targets; only an applied removable scope is a compact token. One inner listbox owns actionable rows; scopes and metadata truncate before controls, every focus state remains visible, and Minimal caps results to measured footer clearance.
components.html: <input class="ds-search" type="text" placeholder="Search everything — open, snoozed, archived, history…" />

narrative.overview: EveryTab is styled the way a great code editor is: the layout, keybindings, density, and component anatomy are fixed and learnable once — and the color scheme is yours. A strict two-axis architecture (data-scheme × data-mode) redefines the same ~14 role tokens per scheme; every component is written once against those roles and never hard-codes a color. Each of 36 built-ins plus every validated custom scheme declares a canonical light or dark presentation for Scheme default; System and forced Light/Dark remain available. The working feel is precise, fast, keyboard-first — Raycast/Linear energy on a warm-paper default.
keyCharacteristics: One fixed structure (full-bleed app shell, sidebar + sticky hero search), 36 built-ins plus validated local custom schemes
All color flows through role tokens; tints, focus rings, and shadows are derived via color-mix, never hand-picked per scheme
Free local custom schemes reuse the same roles: seven guided source colors or the full advanced role map, with strict Light and Dark validation
One fixed public identity layer (deep teal stack plus porcelain / warm ink support) stays recognizable across every product scheme
Crisp and immediate: interactive transitions finish within 180ms; the non-blocking destination locator may hold for 540ms after navigation has completed
Borders and surface tints carry depth; real shadows mean 'this floats'
System font stack only — zero webfont latency, native feel on every OS

rules.name: The Scheme Contract Rule
rules.body: Components never hard-code a color value — only the ~14 scheme roles plus the fixed --brand-* identity roles. Tints, rings, and glows are derived with color-mix from roles. A new scheme is ~10 lines; fixed brand roles are never redefined.

rules.name: The Fixed Identity Rule
rules.body: Public EveryTab marks use the fixed supplied deep-teal stack palette; porcelain and warm ink remain supporting identity colors. Product schemes personalize the interface; they never recolor toolbar or store identity.

rules.name: The Syntax Token Rule
rules.body: Multiple hues are welcome — this is an editor theme, not a monochrome brand system — but every hue must hold a role. Accent acts, accent-strong responds, ok/warn/danger mean. No hue is ever decoration-only in structure.

rules.name: The AA Everywhere Rule
rules.body: Every scheme × mode combination must hold WCAG AA. Verify text against bg-solid, surface, and surface-2; status graphics clear 3:1 and status text clears 4.5:1. Small text on status tints uses --ink.

rules.name: The Custom Scheme Boundary
rules.body: Guided custom schemes own seven source colors per Light and Dark mode; Advanced owns only the production color roles and gradient geometry. Both modes pass the strict component ledger before a UUID record enters Yours. Authoring lives on a dedicated responsive page whose current-theme chrome stays isolated from the draft preview. Built-ins open as exact protected Advanced maps; entering Guided explicitly re-derives roles. Native pickers, editable hex fields, and temporary solid-direct or dashed-derived use highlights do not widen the accepted runtime token boundary. Runtime paint accepts only the 15 allowlisted properties after a validation-seal check; CSS, fonts, images, layout, motion, shape, and brand-token overrides are never accepted.

rules.name: The Tabular Count Rule
rules.body: Every number that can change — sidebar counts, stats line, item meta — sets font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums. Counts must never make the layout breathe.

rules.name: The Float Rule
rules.body: If it doesn't overlap other content, it doesn't get a shadow beyond the whisper. Depth is information: shadow = floating.

dos: Do route every color decision through the ~14 role tokens and derive tints with color-mix — a new scheme must cost ~10 lines and zero component edits.
Do keep one failing custom draft local and resumable, but make only fully validated Light and Dark records usable, portable, shareable, or syncable.
Do use the fixed --brand-* roles for EveryTab identity surfaces and the responsive compact/full mark contract from brainstorm-d2-logo.md.

Do keep interactive transitions within the 80/140/180ms vocabulary with --ease-out; allow only the documented 540ms destination locator after state has completed; keep shared Loading as a solid one-shot reveal and respect prefers-reduced-motion on every animation.
Do keep the structure identical across all built-in and custom schemes: layout, density, hierarchy, and keyboard behavior never move when the palette changes.
Do give every list keyboard access (arrows + Enter, / focuses search) and every focusable a visible ring (--focus-ring, 3–4px). Hit targets ≥ 28px.
Do use font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums on every count, and verify --ink-3 contrast in both modes whenever a scheme is added or touched.
Do express trust in components: undo toast on every automatic action, vault pill always visible, restore always one click.
donts: Don't build hero-metric tiles or put big numbers on the main page — the statsline is one quiet 12.5px line; the stat grid exists only on the dedicated Stats page.
Don't hard-code a color in a component, define per-scheme tints, or introduce an 11th color decision — that breaks the Scheme Contract.
Don't recolor the public toolbar/store mark to match a product scheme; recognition is the mark's job, personalization is the interface's job.
Don't use shadows for at-rest hierarchy. If it doesn't float above other content, it gets a hairline and at most the whisper.

Don't add webfonts, gradient text (background-clip: text), or decorative glassmorphism. The onboarding backdrop blur is the one sanctioned blur; the gradient atmosphere is an opt-in setting, not a default.
Don't use uppercase tracked labels anywhere except the h3/sidebar label role — never as eyebrows above headings.
Don't let a hue exist without a role, and never signal state with color alone — status pills carry text, the vault pill carries a label, danger buttons say what they do.
Don't ship a scheme that fails AA in either mode, and never move UI elements between schemes — 'the user's look follows them, the structure never leaves.'
